sewage-treatment-stages.alt: Flow diagram of a sewage treatment plant from left to right: raw sewage enters screens and a grit chamber, then a primary settling tank where sludge sinks; then an aeration tank where microbes break down organic matter; then tertiary filters that remove nitrogen and phosphorus; then disinfection with chlorine or UV; then clean water is released to a river. Sludge from the tanks goes to a digester that makes methane.
